title: Blisters, Collagen, and a Tight Compartment

questions.stem: Pain out of proportion after a fracture, pain on passive stretch, and a pulse is still present. Next step?

options.text: Wait for the pulse to disappear
Reassure, because a pulse is present

questions.explanation: A pulse can still be there. That does not rule out a tight compartment.

questions.stem: Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis are:

options.text: One peeling drug-rash disease; stop the drug

questions.explanation: The name changes with how much skin peels.

questions.stem: Flaccid blisters and a mouth that is almost always involved. Think:
questions.explanation: Pemphigus splits inside the epidermis. Pemphigoid is tense and subepidermal.

questions.stem: A raised, sharply bordered facial redness is most consistent with:

options.text: Deep cellulitis with a fading edge
A drainable abscess that should only get a longer pill

questions.explanation: Erysipelas is more superficial, raised, and sharp.

questions.stem: In Marfan syndrome, the life-threatening target to measure is:
questions.explanation: The lens goes up, and the aorta is the danger.

questions.stem: Blue sclerae, fractures with little force, and hearing loss suggest:
questions.explanation: Osteogenesis imperfecta. Child protection still stays open.

questions.stem: A missing pulse in suspected compartment syndrome is:

options.text: Proof that fasciotomy can wait overnight
A reason to give only more opioid

questions.explanation: Pain out of proportion and pain on stretch are the early clues.

questions.stem: The first move in a severe peeling drug rash is:

options.text: Stop the drug and treat as a burn
Call it ordinary hives and send the patient home

questions.explanation: Do not re-expose the patient to the culprit.

questions.stem: Blue sclerae in a child with a fracture:

options.text: Do not close a child-protection question; both can be present

questions.explanation: The disease and inflicted injury can coexist.

options.text: Fasciotomy is the treatment of a tight compartment.
A present pulse rules out compartment syndrome.
Pemphigus is flaccid and usually oral.
In Marfan syndrome, measure the aortic root.

questions.explanation: A pulse may still be present; pulselessness is late.
